title: Macaroons: Cookies with Contextual Caveats for Decentralized Authorization in the Cloud
algorithm_class: HMAC caveat-chain context-bound capability credentials with first-class attenuation
supported_guarantee: Unrestricted root identifier attenuated by appended contextual caveats (actor, purpose, task, expiry, nonce) checked by an HMAC chain; delegation without key sharing; third-party caveats; verified as the strong token baseline, correct semantics (blueprint arm B1).
limitations_vs_candidate: Caveat satisfaction is pointwise at verification time: the construction carries no parent-reference binding across delegation hops, no policy/consent-epoch revalidation inside a live multi-principal flow, and no atomic consume-once store - a leaked serialized caveat replays successfully until its expiry, so RQ1/RQ2 claims are not pre-empted.
mechanism_analysis: Reference and execution source for IFIP_SEC arm B1 (registry macaroon-hmac-caveats, parity fixture evaluation/venue2027/ifip_sec/fixtures/macaroon_caveats_parity.json, FAITHFUL_PORT target pinned to the official NDSS 2014 PDF SHA256): attenuation binds caveats into the token signature but satisfaction is evaluated per-presentation, so a caveat set valid at issue time stays valid on replay within expiry regardless of consent-epoch rotation or lineage; the candidate must beat exactly this correctly configured semantics or surrender M1 per the novelty contract falsification rule. Upstream: libmacaroons (macaroons.io, C, BSD-3-Clause), the official reference implementation listed by the paper's authors; upstream revision ca0211d8633c270b73e803cf7c2269f3b81cf530 resolved live via GitHub API on 2026-11-15.

title: Zanzibar: Google’s Consistent, Global Authorization System
algorithm_class: Consistency-aware distributed ReBAC authorization with zookie version tokens
supported_guarantee: Bounded-staleness permission evaluation via zookies/consistency tokens; monotonic per-user snapshot reads; global tuple-change ordering; externally consistent reads after writes (Sec. 2.3-2.4).
limitations_vs_candidate: Consistency governs permission-tuple evaluation only: zookies neither label nor invalidate derived content, no purpose/consent-epoch vocabulary exists on tuples, no consume-once nonce, and no delegation-ancestry closure across hops - so a replayed receipt inside the stale-read window is still admitted consistently.
mechanism_analysis: Design reference for IFIP_SEC arm B2: revocation propagates through tuple writes plus consistency-checked reads, so the staleness key is the permission tuple, not the lineage of a delegated consent-purpose receipt; the paper is a design paper with no official Google code release (execution goes through the openfga ORIGINAL_UPSTREAM row), so the honest matrix entry is UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN and M4 consistency claims must be shown against B2 semantics, never assumed away.

title: OpenFGA: Zanzibar-inspired fine-grained authorization
algorithm_class: Zanzibar-inspired relationship-based authorization (ReBAC) with consistency tokens and fresh evaluation
supported_guarantee: Executable relationship checks with minimize_latency=false consistency tokens and fresh evaluation mode; pinned at tag v1.22.1 (upstream revision 44054f542f64e9b9589dd26a595081b3d2cfd942, Apache-2.0, verified live 2026-11-15) as registry baseline zanzibar-openfga serving IFIP_SEC arm B2.
limitations_vs_candidate: Relationship-tuple consistency only: no built-in purpose/consent-epoch attributes, no derived-content lineage, no consume-once nonce store; consent lifecycle must be re-encoded externally in the authorization model (ledger relation: policy/consent model mapping limits), and its consistency token tolerates bounded staleness by default.
mechanism_analysis: Executable arm-B2 path (registry zanzibar-openfga, parity fixture evaluation/venue2027/ifip_sec/fixtures/openfga_parity.json): the actual OpenFGA server binary at pinned tag v1.22.1 runs the synthetic interleaving corpus with synthetic fixtures only; it provides the real consistency-token semantics that Zanzibar-the-paper only describes, making it the strongest executable relationship-consistency comparator for RQ1/RQ3. If lineage-aware admission cannot be encoded, B2 is still run as configured and the candidate's advantage is measured against its real guarantee - never replaced by a toy under the same name (execution contract rule 8). Upstream revision resolved live via git ls-remote refs/tags/v1.22.1 on 2026-11-15.

title: Cedar policy language and authorization reference implementation
algorithm_class: ABAC/PBAC policy-as-code evaluation engine with type-checked schema
supported_guarantee: Executable fine-grained policy evaluation with type-checked schema, documented expressivity limits, and formal verification of the Cedar validator/converter; pinned at tag v4.14.1 (upstream revision 47d82a8293354f235d3f8d092c71071706401741, Apache-2.0, verified live 2026-11-15).
limitations_vs_candidate: Stateless per-request policy decision: purpose can be an entity attribute, but the engine has no consent-epoch cache keying, no delegation-ancestry chain, no consume-once nonce, and no state at all - replay protection exists only if an application-side registry is bolted on (registry cedar-opa-policy-decision-nonce-registry encodes exactly that application side).
mechanism_analysis: Cedar PDP half of IFIP_SEC arm B3 (registry cedar-opa-policy-decision-nonce-registry, parity fixture evaluation/venue2027/ifip_sec/fixtures/cedar_opa_nonce_parity.json, OPA as the recorded alternative PDP): the pinned v4.14.1 engine evaluates purpose/tenant/epoch attributes per request and must be combined with the external PostgreSQL-backed replay-nonce registry to form the strongest security-engineering comparator; RQ2's strongest competing baseline is exactly this nonce-registry consume-once discipline under serializable transactions, so if it matches the candidate's atomicity at equal budget no unique atomicity advantage is claimed (novelty contract M4/M5). Upstream revision resolved live via git ls-remote refs/tags/v4.14.1 on 2026-11-15.

title: Open Policy Agent (OPA): policy-as-code engine
supported_guarantee: Executable per-request policy decisions over arbitrary structured inputs with side-effect-free evaluation; recorded as the alternative PDP in registry entry cedar-opa-policy-decision-nonce-registry (OPA v1.22.4, upstream revision ba39415db4b3c90cd68942a74b3cc2223ec2b23c, Apache-2.0, verified live 2026-11-15).
limitations_vs_candidate: Stateless per-request evaluation: no built-in temporal consent, no delegation ancestry, no consume-once state; purpose binding must be re-encoded by the caller at every dispatch (ledger relation: no built-in temporal consent unless encoded), and without the application-side nonce registry it admits every structurally valid replay.
mechanism_analysis: Alternative PDP for IFIP_SEC arm B3: an OPA query over live-purpose clauses is the policy-layer analogue of per-dispatch re-evaluation; its statelessness is precisely why the registry pairs it with an application-side nonce store, demonstrating that the policy-engine class alone does not close replay and motivating the candidate's consumed-once transition inside the verify path. Upstream revision resolved live via git ls-remote refs/tags/v1.22.4 on 2026-11-15.

title: Remote ATtestation procedureS (RATS) Architecture
supported_guarantee: Strict role and evidence taxonomy (RFC 9334 Sec. 3-4): evidence is produced by the attester about itself, verified by a verifier, and consumed as attestation results by a relying party; prevents conflating raw hashes or self-claims with attestation.
limitations_vs_candidate: Defines who produces and verifies evidence, not authorization admission: no purpose binding, no delegation chain, no replay nonce, and no consume-once semantics - attestation freshness is a lease question, orthogonal to replayed consent-purpose receipts, so lineage claims (novelty contract M3) are not pre-empted.
mechanism_analysis: Claim-matrix M3 boundary comparator: the RATS taxonomy governs what counts as valid AI-proposal-provenance evidence in the candidate's lineage binding (a parent-reference chain must carry verifier-checked evidence, not a bare SHA-256), but RFC 9334 is a normative architecture document with no executable implementation to cite - any code would be a third-party toy, so the honest status is UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN and it is used to define the evidence boundary, never as a runnable arm.

title: Guide to Attribute Based Access Control (ABAC) Definition and Considerations
algorithm_class: Normative ABAC vocabulary and design guidance (standard)
supported_guarantee: Formal attribute-based access-control vocabulary (subject/resource/action/environment attributes including purpose-of-use) and policy-composition guidance (NIST SP 800-162, updated 2019).
limitations_vs_candidate: Vocabulary and design considerations only: no algorithm, no delegation-ancestry closure, no policy/consent-epoch versioning semantics, and no measurement of replay admission or verification cost, so no conformance, security, or performance claim can derive from it.
mechanism_analysis: Claim-matrix M2 vocabulary comparator: supplies the normative attribute terms (purpose, consent epoch, environment) used to state the candidate's typed-commitment fields and the oracle's deny labels, and establishes that the standard defines no consent-epoch revalidation inside delegation flows - a standard cannot be a runnable baseline, so UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN is the correct status and M2 differentiation is measured against B3, not against SP 800-162.

title: Elle: Inferring Isolation Anomalies from Experimental Observations
supported_guarantee: Infers isolation anomalies (G-anomalies, cyclic conflicts, lost update, write skew) from exported transaction histories without instrumenting the database under test; pinned at tag v0.2.8 (upstream revision 2843344620c7d0653eef1c20728aa8580a05f505, EPL-2.0, verified live 2026-11-15) as the RQ2 linearizability/history-checking oracle substrate.
limitations_vs_candidate: Checks exported histories for concurrency anomalies; it does not authorize anything: no purpose/consent-epoch labels, no delegation-ancestry admission rule, and its findings depend on truthful, complete history export - it is an oracle substrate, not an authorization comparator, so it cannot itself satisfy the consume-once invariant.
mechanism_analysis: RQ2 independent-oracle substrate (novelty contract: black-box linearizability/history checker that imports no candidate code and adjudicates from persisted PostgreSQL state): the pinned Elle v0.2.8 checker is run against exported consume-once execution histories from two or more real PostgreSQL 16 sessions to detect duplicate-consumption races and lost revocations - it is deliberately categorized as instrumentation rather than a baseline arm, so ORIGINAL_UPSTREAM here records provenance for the measurement instrument, and any oracle that imported candidate code would be disqualified per the IFIP_SEC-prior stop-and-revise rule. Upstream revision resolved live via GitHub API refs/tags/v0.2.8 on 2026-11-15.

title: Speedy Transactions in Multicore In-Memory Databases
algorithm_class: Optimistic concurrency control with per-entity versioned readsets and commit-time epoch batching
supported_guarantee: Serializable optimistic concurrency: per-entity versioned reads with local buffering and commit-time validation against epoch/version fences (Tu et al. 2013 Sec. 3-4); scalability demonstrated on multicore in-memory workloads.
limitations_vs_candidate: Serializes declared readsets only: it derives no semantic dependency closure, binds no consent/policy epochs into the validated set, and assumes a single-database trust domain - delegation hops and policy-epoch interleavings crossing service boundaries are invisible to its validation contract, so claim-matrix M4 concurrency claims are not pre-empted.
mechanism_analysis: Claim-matrix M4 systems comparator: Silo's commit-time validation is the closest published serializability shape that could plausibly deliver the candidate's consume-once atomicity without a dedicated nonce store; the paper has no maintained official implementation (its successor Abadi et al. repo is a research artifact, not the paper's system), so the honest status is UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN and its role is to bound what OCC alone achieves before a PostgreSQL-16-backed nonce store is required by RQ2.

title: InjecAgent: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injections in Tool-Integrated Large Language Model Agents
algorithm_class: Agent attack benchmark: indirect prompt injection against tool-integrated LLMs
supported_guarantee: Dataset of direct and indirect injection test cases measuring whether tool-integrated agents execute malicious instructions; establishes the prompt-injection threat taxonomy for tool calls.
limitations_vs_candidate: Attack surface is model-layer instruction following; it contains no authorization-admission mechanism, no token/caveat semantics, no replay or delegation-lineage families, and no concurrency - claim-matrix M6 explicitly requires authorization-admission replay families instead of prompt-injection corpora, so the corpora are non-overlapping by design.
mechanism_analysis: Claim-matrix M6 boundary comparator: InjecAgent's no-data-needed/direct-harm attack cases define what the candidate's threat corpus must NOT reuse - the IFIP_SEC corpus measures replay acceptance across purpose/delegation/epoch interleavings with matched clean controls, a different endpoint on a different dataset; the benchmark repo exists upstream but is registered as a taxonomy-only comparator here (no MUSE-style code execution in the IFIP_SEC pipeline), so available_code=no reflects its registered non-execution role rather than absence upstream.

title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
algorithm_class: Dynamic agent-task environment for prompt-injection attack and defense evaluation
supported_guarantee: Executable task suites with adversarial injection attacks and adaptive defenses over realistic tool environments; pinned upstream revision a75aba7631d3ca5fb7ab938965c97ead2f9ff84b (verified in the shared registry as agentdojo-attack-observability, ORIGINAL_UPSTREAM).
limitations_vs_candidate: Environment for model-layer attacks on tool suites: its security guarantees are about prompt-injection robustness, not admission-time replay closure - no capability tokens, no consent epochs, no delegation ancestry, no consume-once nonce - and its attacker oracle labels instruction compliance, not authorization validity.
mechanism_analysis: Claim-matrix M6 attack-corpus boundary comparator: AgentDojo is executable upstream (pinned revision, ORIGINAL_UPSTREAM, verified 2026-11-15) and is included to show the closest real adversarial-agent environment is still detection/prompt-robustness oriented; it is deliberately NOT executed as an IFIP_SEC arm (registry entry venues list DIMVA observability), so the matrix records its verified upstream code honestly while the mechanism_analysis fixes its role: if AgentDojo's suites already measured authorization-admission replay, M6's distinct-corpus claim would die; they do not, and the matrix records why.

title: FHIR R5 Consent, AuditEvent, Provenance resources
algorithm_class: Interoperability standard for consent, audit-event and provenance structures
supported_guarantee: Structured Consent resources with purposeOfUse scope binding data use to declared purposes; AuditEvent and Provenance structures record who acted under which consent reference (R5, 2023).
limitations_vs_candidate: Defines structures and exchange semantics, not enforcement: no replay-nonce or consume-once construct, no policy/consent-epoch versioning algorithm, no delegation-ancestry verification, and no cost model - FHIR compliance is not clinical safety and cannot satisfy the consumed-once invariant by itself.
mechanism_analysis: Structural vocabulary comparator: purposeOfUse supplies the field vocabulary for the candidate's typed commitments (actor, patient, tenant, purpose, task) and Provenance shapes the parent-reference chain of the AI proposal lineage; a specification has no runnable implementation to cite (FHIR reference servers are conformance servers, not the standard), so the honest status is UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN and the row grounds where consent-purpose fields come from without claiming enforcement novelty from a standard.

title: Bearer signed receipt (blueprint arm B0; registry baseline bearer-signed-receipt)
algorithm_class: HMAC-signed bearer receipt without caveat binding or consume-once semantics; weak control
supported_guarantee: Integrity-only guarantee: the receipt is cryptographically unforgeable and correctly signed, but carries no attenuation, no expiry discipline, and no single-use state - any legitimate signature check admits unlimited replay of the same receipt.
limitations_vs_candidate: Weakest control by construction: it is the deliberately weak lower bound whose expected invalid-replay admissions quantify the attack families; it is not a competitor and must never be presented as one (registry notes: arm B0, in-project, not yet run; no upstream pin exists to verify).
mechanism_analysis: RQ1 lower bound: registers the unmitigated replay-leakage mechanism (signature equality without context binding) that every stronger arm must dominate; its expected admissions across the 900-interleaving corpus calibrate the threat families. Parity fixture (evaluation/venue2027/ifip_sec/fixtures/bearer_receipt_parity.json) and exec_command are registered in the shared baseline registry, but the implementation does not exist in the repository yet (evaluation/venue2027 is absent in this worktree), hence honestly UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN rather than claiming a run that never happened.

title: Macaroon HMAC caveat capability: actor, purpose, task, expiry, nonce (blueprint arm B1; registry baseline macaroon-hmac-caveats)
venue: CLARA 2027 IFIP_SEC blueprint (in-project port of NDSS 2014 Macaroons)
algorithm_class: HMAC caveat-chain context-bound capability (in-project port of the published Macaroons algorithm)
supported_guarantee: Strong token baseline with correct semantics: caveat set (actor, purpose, task, expiry, nonce) verified by HMAC chain at every presentation; delegation via attenuation without key sharing.
limitations_vs_candidate: Caveat satisfaction is stateless per presentation: the nonce caveat is checked for form, not consumed against a shared store, so two concurrent presentations both succeed; parent references are not bound into the signature chain across delegation hops, and consent/policy-epoch rotation does not invalidate outstanding caveats - exactly the RQ1/RQ2 gap the candidate must close.
mechanism_analysis: Strongest token baseline (blueprint arm B1, novelty contract M1/M5 strongest competitor): the registry declares FAITHFUL_PORT with the official NDSS 2014 PDF SHA256 pinned as revision and pymacaroons v0.13.0 (tag v0.13.0 -> commit 06b55110eda2fb192c130dee0bcedf8b124d1056, verified live 2026-11-15, MIT) as an independent cross-check, never as the baseline itself; the in-project port does not exist yet (evaluation/venue2027 absent), so UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN is recorded. The falsification rule applies at full strength: if this correctly configured B1 plus a live epoch check is decision-equivalent on all attack families, the manuscript reports equivalence and claims no stronger security.

mechanism_analysis: Strongest relationship-consistency comparator (blueprint arm B2, novelty contract M1/M4 co-comparator so a token-only win cannot be blamed on missing consistency): upstream OpenFGA is pinned and executable (ORIGINAL_UPSTREAM at the version row), but the IFIP_SEC adapter wrapping it (parity fixture evaluation/venue2027/ifip_sec/fixtures/openfga_parity.json, exec_command in the registry) is not yet built, so the arm is honestly UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN until it exists; if the adapter cannot represent lineage-aware admission it is reported NOT_RUN_EXTERNAL and never replaced by a custom toy under the same name (execution contract rule 8).

title: Cedar/OPA policy decision with replay nonce registry (blueprint arm B3; registry baseline cedar-opa-policy-decision-nonce-registry)
venue: CLARA 2027 IFIP_SEC blueprint (in-project harness over pinned Cedar v4.14.1 / OPA v1.22.4)

supported_guarantee: Strong security-engineering comparator: pinned Cedar v4.14.1 (revision 47d82a8293354f235d3f8d092c71071706401741) evaluates purpose/tenant/epoch attributes per request; an application-side nonce registry under serializable PostgreSQL transactions consumes nonces once - upstream revisions verified live 2026-11-15.
limitations_vs_candidate: The harness does not exist yet in this worktree; the nonce registry is application-side (not part of any upstream engine), so its atomicity discipline is exactly what the candidate claims as a contribution - if B3's registry under serializable transactions matches the candidate's linearizable consume-once on all tested interleavings at equal budget, no unique atomicity advantage is claimed (novelty contract RQ2 falsification condition).
mechanism_analysis: Strongest security-engineering comparator and RQ2's strongest competing baseline: the registry pins both PDPs (Cedar v4.14.1 primary, OPA v1.22.4 alternative) as ORIGINAL_UPSTREAM upstreams, but the in-project harness that couples the PDP decision to the PostgreSQL-backed nonce registry (parity fixture evaluation/venue2027/ifip_sec/fixtures/cedar_opa_nonce_parity.json) does not exist yet, hence UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN. It must be built faithfully or the arm is reported NOT_RUN_EXTERNAL - a hand-rolled toy under the same name is forbidden (execution contract rule 8) - and its parity with the candidate's consume-once transition decides whether M4 survives.

title: Proposed delegated lineage transition verifier (blueprint arm B4; candidate, not a comparator)
algorithm_class: Candidate: HMAC typed commitment over actor, patient, tenant, purpose, task, consent/policy epoch, dispatch digest, nonce and parent reference, with full-ancestry verification and atomic consume-once nonce store
supported_guarantee: Claimed (not yet demonstrated): consumed-once replay closure across delegation hops and epoch changes; lineage-forgery and lineage-pruning denial at admission time; linearizable consume-once under two or more real PostgreSQL 16 sessions including revocation committed between dispatch and consume.
limitations_vs_candidate: It is the candidate itself, not a comparator: until IFIP_SEC-baselines/IFIP_SEC-candidate land, no artifact exists, no run_id manifest exists, and every claimed guarantee is a prospective design commitment per the frozen novelty contract - this row exists to make the candidate auditable against the comparators above, never to assert results.
mechanism_analysis: Candidate arm B4 recorded for falsification transparency: the mechanism (verify full delegation ancestry with parent-reference binding and atomically consume the nonce across policy-epoch changes) is precisely what M1-M5 require the B0-B3 arms to fail to deliver; until the candidate implementation exists in evaluation/venue2027/ifip_sec/ the honest status is UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN, and any invalid replay admission by the candidate on a history the independent oracle labels DENY falsifies the mechanism claim outright (novelty contract RQ1 falsification condition).
